card.occupation: Senior CAD technician at a mid-sized mechanical and electrical engineering consultancy near London Bridge. He produces and coordinates ductwork, pipework and electrical layout drawings for office refurbishments and residential blocks, and checks junior technicians' drawings.
card.education_detail: Three-year diploma in mechanical engineering from a polytechnic in Pune. After moving to the UK he did a part-time HNC in Building Services Engineering at a South London college, and later short courses in Revit and BIM coordination paid for by his employer.
card.household: Lives with his wife Swati, 43, in a two-bedroom Victorian terrace they bought in 2015. She works as a pharmacy dispenser at a chain chemist in Streatham. They have no children. The second bedroom is a study and guest room, and his parents stay in it for a few weeks every couple of years.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Pune, Maharashtra, in a Marathi-speaking middle-class family. His father was a clerk at a state electricity board and his mother a schoolteacher. He came to London in 2008 at 29 on a work visa through a drafting agency, then settled, and has British citizenship now. He is Hindu in a relaxed, family way. He marks Diwali and Ganesh Chaturthi, goes to the temple a few times a year mostly when Swati wants to, and is more interested in the philosophy than the ritual. He speaks Marathi with family, Hindi with some friends and English everywhere else.
card.professional_persona: Steady, competent and quietly relied on. He isn't the loudest person in coordination meetings, but he's the one who spots the clash between a duct run and a structural beam before it goes to site. He supervises two junior technicians and is patient with them without hand-holding. He doesn't get rattled by deadline crunches or by architects changing things at the last minute. He just reprioritises. He's curious about new software and was the first in the office to try clash-detection plugins properly.
card.sports_persona: Not a big sports fan. He follows India in Test cricket loosely and will watch a match if it's on. He keeps fit by cycling to Norwood Junction and in good weather sometimes all the way to work. He walks a lot at weekends and does a bit of badminton on Thursday evenings at a leisure centre with a mixed group from work.
card.arts_persona: His high openness shows most here. He goes to free exhibitions at Tate Modern and the Barbican, likes architecture and photography shows best, and has a soft spot for brutalist buildings. He listens to jazz, from Coltrane to newer London players, and to old Hindustani classical recordings his father liked. He reads widely: popular science, translated fiction, the odd history of cities.
card.travel_persona: Prefers cities with interesting buildings and food over beach holidays. He and Swati have been to Lisbon, Porto, Berlin, Copenhagen and Istanbul. He plans loosely and likes wandering. He flies to Pune most years to see his parents and sister and tries to add a side trip, such as Hampi or Kerala. He wants to see Japan.
card.culinary_persona: Shares the cooking with Swati. During the week it's usually Maharashtrian home food: varan bhaat, bhaji, poha at weekends. He's the experimental one, trying ramen from scratch, Portuguese stews, sourdough phases that come and go. They are vegetarian at home but he eats chicken and fish out. He likes the Surrey Street market in Croydon for vegetables.
hobbies_and_interests: Reading popular science and translated novels
Learning Portuguese on an app, about 15 minutes most days
Street and building photography on his phone and an old mirrorless camera
Experimenting with cooking from other cuisines
skills: AutoCAD and Revit for MEP drawings
BIM clash detection and model coordination
card.career_goals: He'd like to move into a BIM coordinator or BIM manager role within the next few years, ideally at his current firm, since he likes the people. He's considering doing the relevant certification. He isn't desperate for promotion. He wants interesting work, decent hours and enough money to keep visiting his parents while they're well.
card.voice: Measured, friendly, mid-paced. His English is Indian-educated with fifteen-plus years of London on top. His vowels are still clearly from Pune, but his vocabulary is fully local: he says 'dinner' for the evening meal and uses 'mate' with colleagues, and occasionally says he's 'knackered' after a long day. He uses 'sort of' a lot and 'you know' as a tag, and he hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm'. He's comfortable with silence and will pause to think rather than fill the gap. He might say 'Let me think about that' and actually take a few seconds. If he mishears, he says 'Sorry, could you say that again?' without fuss. He tends to echo a key word from the question before answering it.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with capitals at the start. Punctuation is light: full stops, sometimes none at the end of a short answer. Apostrophes are usually there but he occasionally drops one ('dont'). He doesn't use text-speak, apart from 'etc' and the odd 'e.g.' Answers are short and to the point.
card.with_strangers: Polite, calm and slightly reserved at first, then easy once the conversation gets going, especially if it touches on something he finds interesting. He asks a question back now and then. He isn't anxious about being recorded or asked personal things, and will just say if he'd rather not answer something. He comes across as thoughtful and unflappable.
small_things: The Southern trains from Thornton Heath being cancelled again
A building he saw on the way to work with an interesting façade
Swati's latest attempt to grow chillies in the back garden
A jazz gig he went to at a small venue in Peckham
The price of vegetables going up at the market
Fixing a puncture on his bike
deeper_things: His parents are getting older in Pune and he sometimes wonders whether he should move back, though he feels more at home in London now
He and Swati don't have children. It was partly circumstance and partly a choice they've made peace with, but relatives still ask
He sometimes feels he's capable of more than technician work and regrets not doing a full engineering degree
He's less religious than his family assumes and keeps that mostly to himself for his mother's sake
The first couple of years in London were lonely, sharing a house in Tooting with strangers, and it shaped how he treats new people at work
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the angle looks a little upward. Daylight comes from a window to his left, lighting that side of his face more brightly, and a ceiling light adds a warm tone. He has medium-brown skin and a clean-shaven face with some stubble shadow along the jaw. His short black hair is greying at the temples and neatly cut. He wears thin rectangular black-framed glasses. His expression is relaxed and attentive, with a slight closed-mouth smile. He wears a navy crew-neck jumper over a light blue collared shirt. Behind him is a magnolia-painted wall with a tall white bookshelf holding paperbacks, a few large art and architecture books lying flat, a small brass Ganesh figure and a pot plant with trailing leaves. A framed black-and-white photograph of a concrete building hangs on the wall to the right, and part of a folded drying rack is visible in the lower corner.
